description: Describe how generative AI models work at an intuitive, non-mathematical level, including Introduction to the Generative AI Landscape, What generative AI is and isn't, From single models to multi-model systems, Foundations and Intuition of Generative Models, Discriminative vs generative models, Attention, intuitively.
Apply prompt engineering techniques to obtain useful, reliable outputs from generative models, including Prompt Engineering Fundamentals, Advanced Prompt Engineering, Evaluation, Prompt Engineering.

Build a small generative AI application end to end, retrieval-augmented generation, structured output validation, basic agent/tool use, and an appropriate customization strategy (prompting, RAG, or fine-tuning), including Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), Why grounding matters, the RAG pipeline, RAG evaluation and failure modes, Building Generative AI Applications, Agents and Tool Use, When NOT to use an agent, Model Customization.

Evaluate generative AI outputs and systems using rubrics, test sets, model-as-judge methods, and analysis of failure modes, including Model-as-judge with verification, Building Generative AI Applications, Evaluation, Failure Modes.
Analyze the ethical, social, legal, and governance implications of generative AI and apply responsible-use practices, including Society, Law, Governance, Governance inside organisations.
